title: The Beauty of the Dream Vanished
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Frankenstein by Mary Shelley (1818).
body: It was on a dreary night of November that I beheld the accomplishment of my toils. With an anxiety that almost amounted to agony, I collected the instruments of life around me, that I might infuse a spark of being into the lifeless thing that lay at my feet. It was already one in the morning; the rain pattered dismally against the panes, and my candle was nearly burnt out, when, by the glimmer of the half-extinguished light, I saw the dull yellow eye of the creature open; it breathed hard, and a convulsive motion agitated its limbs.

How can I describe my emotions at this catastrophe, or how delineate the wretch whom with such infinite pains and care I had endeavoured to form? His limbs were in proportion, and I had selected his features as beautiful. Beautiful! Great God! His yellow skin scarcely covered the work of muscles and arteries beneath; his hair was of a lustrous black, and flowing; his teeth of a pearly whiteness; but these luxuriances only formed a more horrid contrast with his watery eyes, that seemed almost of the same colour as the dun-white sockets in which they were set, his shrivelled complexion and straight black lips.

The different accidents of life are not so changeable as the feelings of human nature. I had worked hard for nearly two years, for the sole purpose of infusing life into an inanimate body. For this I had deprived myself of rest and health. I had desired it with an ardour that far exceeded moderation; but now that I had finished, the beauty of the dream vanished, and breathless horror and disgust filled my heart.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, on what kind of night did the narrator behold the accomplishment of his toils?
Per the passage, what time was it when the creature's eye opened?
According to the passage, what color were the creature's eyes when they opened?
Per the passage, how had the narrator selected the creature's features?
According to the passage, what color was the creature's hair?
Per the passage, how long had the narrator worked for the sole purpose of infusing life into an inanimate body?
Based on the passage, why does the narrator exclaim "Beautiful! Great God!" right after describing his choice of beautiful features?
options: He is struck with horror at how wrong his expectations were, since the result is monstrous rather than beautiful
He is genuinely pleased and proud of how the creature turned out
He is mocking the creature's appearance for comic effect
He is praising God for helping him complete the work successfully

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the narrator say "the beauty of the dream vanished" once he had finished his work?
options: Now that the creation was real and complete, horror replaced the idealistic excitement he had felt while pursuing it
He realized the entire project had been a waste of money
He discovered that the creature could not actually move at all
He had lost interest in science entirely after the experiment

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the overall point of the passage?
options: The narrator's long-desired creation comes to life, but the reality horrifies him instead of fulfilling his dream
The narrator is delighted with his creation and celebrates his success
The narrator abandons his experiment before it can be completed
The narrator describes a peaceful, uneventful night with no unusual events

questions.prompt: As used in the passage, what does it mean that "a convulsive motion agitated its limbs"?
options: Its limbs jerked or twitched suddenly and uncontrollably
Its limbs moved slowly and gracefully
Its limbs were bound tightly together

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what was the narrator's emotional state as he collected the instruments of life?
options: Anxiety that almost amounted to agony

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what was happening to the narrator's candle as the creature came to life?
options: It had just been freshly lit
It had already gone out completely

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the narrator say scarcely covered the muscles and arteries beneath it?
Per the passage, what did the narrator deprive himself of during his two years of work?
Based on the passage, why does the narrator contrast the creature's "lustrous black" hair and "pearly" teeth with its watery eyes and shrivelled complexion?
options: To show that individually beautiful features combined into an overall horrifying, unnatural appearance
To prove that the creature had no beautiful features at all
To argue that hair and teeth are more important than eyes
To suggest that the creature's appearance would improve over time

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes the shift in the narrator's feelings described in the passage?
options: His long pursuit of a beautiful dream turns to horror and disgust the moment it is actually realized
His feelings remain calm and unchanged from beginning to end
He feels growing pride and satisfaction as the passage continues
He becomes increasingly confused about what he has actually created

questions.prompt: As used in the passage, what does it mean that the narrator had desired his creation with "an ardour that far exceeded moderation"?
options: An intense passion or eagerness well beyond what was reasonable
A mild, casual interest that came and went
A fear so strong it prevented him from acting
A calm, carefully measured, and reasonable desire
